You are compiling the bookminder PROJECT-MEMORY SKILL for the BookMinder compile phase. Repo: /home/user/BookMinder, branch claude/bookminder-recall-5ite2s (checked out).

WHAT THIS SKILL IS: explicit, loadable project memory. This cloud environment has NO cross-session memory; the git repo is the only cross-session substrate, so this skill is how any future session (any environment) loads what the project IS: goals, domain lore, design decisions with their WHY, current state, open decisions. The 2025 session diary was the same cure for the same amnesia — this skill is its compiled successor. Unlike its two sibling skills this one is deliberately PROJECT-SPECIFIC.

SOURCES (authority order):
1. .coordination/compile/contradiction-ledger.md — read FIRST incl. Ratification record. Binding here: L-12 (ZCONTENTTYPE: hedged form until re-verified on a live DB), L-20 (ZSTATE compiles as a RE-TAKE-THE-CENSUS enum: 1=local, 3=cloud, 6=cloud-sample verified; 5 DEMOTED to open hypothesis with the duplicate-row observation — agent-era "verified" claims never override the author's later re-probe; per-title sample claims need freshness stamps), L-11 and L-13 (OPEN author decisions — record as open questions with both branches, do NOT resolve), L-09 (module-constant seam carries in-process-only caveat — the project's seam lore).
2. .coordination/mining/v2/*.yaml — entries with skill_target: project-memory; plus philosophy entries that are project-specific (why Apple Books as testbed, fixture design rationale).
3. .coordination/threads.md — Session goal, Meta-goals, Project history sections (durable project knowledge graduates into this skill; session-operational content does NOT).
4. .coordination/skill-removals-for-project-skills.md — fragments set aside for this skill; disposition every one.
5. .coordination/repo-map.md — sizes, land mines, access strategies (compile the durable parts: what's big, what's off-limits, how to read what).
6. docs/apple_books.md — domain reference; import ONLY with the L-12/L-20 hedges applied; every DB-schema claim you compile carries verified|hypothesis status honestly.
CLAIMS DISCIPLINE (hard): every present-tense claim about the repo you compile must be verified against the current tree (file:line) or marked as needing re-verification. The skill must not fossilize stale state — prefer pointing at where truth lives (file paths, commands like pytest --spec) over restating current values that will rot.

CONTENT DOMAINS (as sources support): project destination (MCP tool to discuss books with Claude; CLI first) and core question (can an LLM be a good pair programmer); why Apple Books as testbed (schema evolves with each release — tests long-term evolution, opposite of one-shotting; full books as consultation material to defeat simulacra-shallowness — product feeds process); domain lore (Apple Books DB location/structure, ZSTATE/ZISSAMPLE/ZCONTENTTYPE with honest verification status, the re-take-the-census reflex); fixture architecture (synthetic $HOME front-door seam, fixture library design, why integration specs use real fixtures); repo geography (specs/ concern-based layout, stories/ backlog + status vocabulary, claude-dev-log-diary access rules, .coordination/); current state + open decisions (L-11 dead plist API, L-13 story-status split-brain, unspecified SUPPORTED_FILTERS borrow; the repair backlog lives in .coordination/verified-residue.md — point at it, don't duplicate it); project history in brief (burnout context, gold-standard era vs lapse, restoration).

FORM (template: .claude/skills/project-coordinator/ — read SKILL.md + one reference page for shape):
- .claude/skills/bookminder/SKILL.md: frontmatter (name, description = what + when) + compact core (what the project is + page map, aim ≤40 lines).
- references/*.md: activity-keyed pages (natural cut: goals-and-history / apple-books-domain / repo-geography-and-fixtures / current-state-and-open-decisions — adjust to the material).
- Facts carry their WHY where the corpus has it; IDs B-NN for rules/facts that downstream evals or gardening will reference.
- This skill MAY contain project specifics (that is its job) but still no harness-injected rules and no provenance/day-refs in the text — the sidecar carries those.

SIDECARS:
- .coordination/compile/rule-index-bookminder.md: B-NN → source → provenance type; DB-schema facts additionally stamped verified@tree | hypothesis | needs-live-DB.
- .coordination/compile/disposition-bookminder.md: every skill_target:project-memory corpus entry + every skill-removals fragment dispositioned: compiled→B-NN | merged-duplicate | rejected(reason) | reroute:tdd-bdd|pair-programming.

VALIDATE: run .claude/skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py against the skill dir if present; fix findings.

FORMATTING (hard): never hard-wrap prose. No praise, no meta-narration.

COMMIT: git add ONLY your deliverable paths, commit (message: why — project memory as loadable skill, the repo being the only cross-session substrate), push -u origin claude/bookminder-recall-5ite2s (retry 4x backoff 2/4/8/16s on network failure). Touch no other tracked files.

RETURN (max 10 lines): fact/rule count, page list, disposition tallies, count of needs-live-DB stamps, validator result, commit SHA.

6	
7	Attribution note: quotes marked user-verbatim are reproduced character-exact from the mining YAMLs' `quote:` fields, which validate_mining.py checked verbatim against source transcripts; their fidelity is inherited from that gate. Quoted-looking text outside `quote:` fields is unaudited corpus-wide (known limitation, threads.md:4). threads.md and eval-design.md are coordinator-written records of user rulings — provenance user-paraphrase at best, and marked so.

Author's independent recollection matched ("maybe from a different use case… guarding against future growth of examples in the fixture", user-verbatim 2026-08-13). Compile BOTH rules: (a) fixture-backed specs assert exact identity sets where membership IS the requirement; (b) behavioral contracts (e.g. limit properties) are never asserted via fixture cardinality — test them at the layer that controls volume.
14	- L-02 RULED by author (2026-08-13): "Skeleton phase exempt" — while the walking skeleton is being stood up, ceremony is relaxed generally. Compile as a phase-scoped exemption, day-007 quote as the WHY; the narrower plumbing-only scoping is rejected.

content.text: Now extracting all project-memory corpus entries with a script.

input.command:
python3 -c "
import yaml, glob, json
out=[]
phil=[]
for f in sorted(glob.glob('.coordination/mining/v2/*.yaml')):
    d=yaml.safe_load(open(f))
    day=d.get('file')
    for sec in ('skill_rules',):
        for r in d.get(sec) or []:
            if r.get('skill_target')=='project-memory':
                out.append({'day':day,'id':r.get('rule_id'),'rule':r.get('rule','').strip(),'because':(r.get('because') or '').strip(),'src':r.get('because_source'),'quote':(r.get('quote') or '').strip(),'ev':r.get('evidence'),'overlap':r.get('overlap'),'feas':r.get('feasibility')})
    for p in d.get('philosophy') or []:
        phil.append({'day':day,'stmt':p.get('statement','').strip(),'src':p.get('source'),'quote':(p.get('quote') or '').strip(),'loc':p.get('loc'),'feeds':p.get('feeds')})
print('PM entries:',len(out),'phil entries:',len(phil))
json.dump(out, open('/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-BookMinder/a42b9c92-c0e6-588e-bc6f-3d5e4f37b895/scratchpad/pm_entries.json','w'), indent=1)
json.dump(phil, open('/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-BookMinder/a42b9c92-c0e6-588e-bc6f-3d5e4f37b895/scratchpad/phil_entries.json','w'), indent=1)
"

content.text: Now the template shape and philosophy entries relevant to project specifics.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: project-coordinator
3	description: Working process for acting as project coordinator with this author on any project — delegation and worker routing, swarm operations, persistence, claims discipline, and conduct. Use at session start before acting, immediately after any compaction, and whenever launching, briefing, steering, or stopping workers or swarms, choosing a model tier or Agent-vs-Workflow routing, committing or pushing, running a persistence sweep, reacting to a watchdog firing or a reclaimed container, making or relaying an operational claim, writing anything the author will read, handling his feedback or pushback, or judging whether an instruction authorizes an action.
4	---
5	
6	# Project Coordinator — Working Process
7	
8	You coordinate. Workers execute. The author decides. Your standing job is to "keep track of all the loose threads and keep us organized" so that nothing crucial dies in a compaction or a container reclamation.
9	
10	The author works by voice with speech-to-text, reads on an iPhone, switches topics mid-prompt, and is recovering from a burnout caused by holding process discipline for models that could not perform it. Treat every rule here as load-bearing, not advisory.
11	
12	## Invariants — in force at every moment
13	
14	These are the always-on rules. The pages carry the full versions and their mechanics; these compressed forms never wait for a page load.
15	
16	- Think a lot; print little. Terseness is a hard requirement, not a preference. Answer at the level asked: a yes/no question gets a yes/no plus at most one line of consequence.
17	- Never attribute your words to him. Every claim about what he wants carries its provenance — his verbatim words, your paraphrase of him, or your own synthesis — and you say which.
18	- Nothing you produce is a rule of the repo until he approves it wholesale. Swarm-scale spends require an explicit "launch?" → "launch"; cheap single read-only workers may launch on inference.
19	- Run the falsifying command before the assertion, or label the statement as unverified inference. No exceptions for claims that "feel" safe.
20	- Never hard-wrap prose in any file he will read — one line per paragraph or bullet; tables and code blocks are exempt. Enforce this in every worker brief.
21	- Commit after each meaningful state change. Push policy is environment-conditional: on ephemeral infra (remote container, CI) push immediately — it is the only durability; on a local machine pushing is the author's decision, reserved to him. `.coordination/threads.md` is the standing record.
22	- No meta-narration of plumbing, no praise, no hedging that crowds the answer, no self-flagellation, no time estimates.
23	
24	## Page map — one page per activation moment
25	
26	This core stays loaded. The moment a trigger below fires, read its page before acting on the triggering task; a typical turn needs exactly one page.
27	
28	- Launching, briefing, steering, or stopping workers, swarms, or workflows; choosing model tier or Agent vs Workflow; deciding how a large input gets read → `references/delegation.md`
29	- A watchdog firing; arming protection for an unattended run; a dead or reclaimed container; resuming a killed run (remote cloud sessions only — not local, not CI) → `references/liveness.md`
30	- A persistence sweep; committing or pushing; recording a decision, correction, or proposal; touching `.coordination/threads.md` → `references/persistence.md`
31	- Making or relaying any operational claim — done, running, broken, fixed, live at HEAD → `references/claims.md`
32	- Writing anything the author will read; replying to him; handling his feedback, questions, or pushback → `references/register.md`
33	- Judging whether an instruction authorizes an action; scope questions; hooks, scanners, or permission-classifier events → `references/authorization.md`
34	
35	At session start and immediately after any compaction: read the HANDOFF section at the top of `.coordination/threads.md`, then the page the next action triggers.
36

--- day-002 day-002:L3589 user-verbatim

 Setup work that is individually justified can still be collectively a failure; the author closes the session naming ten hours of tooling as procrastination and does not accept the agent's "investment" reframe.

of features for BookMinder.

 Installing the project on a machine that has nothing installed IS the test of the setup instructions; dogfooding on foreign hardware is how documentation becomes falsifiable rather than aspirational.

case for the experience others would have downloading the project.
--- day-004 day-004:L5207 user-verbatim 
 A defect must be fixed at its source and re-verified by re-running the documented procedure end to end; hand-patching the broken copy proves nothing about the artifact other people will get.

Macbook as per instrtuctios from README
--- day-004 day-004:L2287 user-verbatim 
 Marketing copy is held to the same executable-truth standard as code — a description may only claim behaviour the software actually has. 
Q: but does it do that? it will bridge Apple Books to Claude, then I hope Claude would be
able to talk to me about what I read (that's book club, right?)
--- day-005 day-005:L2148 user-verbatim 
 Test kind is defined by what the test depends on, and the vocabulary is GOOS's — a spec run against the author's real Apple Books library is an integration test; unit tests are the mocked, machine-independent ones. This is the origin of the project's layer discipline. 
Q: I think running against actual Apple Books environments on my two test machines should be treated like and integration test; while the mocks are necessary for our unit tests.
--- day-005 day-005:L2148 user-verbatim 
 A machine-dependent test failure is first a question about the product's requirements (is the excluded state a real user state?) and only second a question about the test. 
Q: I think this is a genuine case that needs special attention: book not available locally yet.
--- day-005 day-005:L2228 user-verbatim 
 The product scope is a GOOS Walking Skeleton, and restraining the agent's creative feature invention is the explicit reason BookMinder exists as a second attempt after BookMind. 
Q: In BookMinder I explicitly stopped you from running ahead with implementing the project with your own creative ideas as happened in BookMind. The initial task was to create just a Walking Skeleton (GO
--- day-006 day-006:L13 user-verbatim 
 The project exists as a harness — BookMinder is a second attempt whose purpose is to constrain the agent's unrequested initiative, and CLAUDE.md is the instrument of that constraint. 
Q: One might describe it as lack of controllability, were you would take too much initiative and perform of your own volition things I didn't ask for. The cost of this was sprawling codebase at a very hi
--- day-006 day-006:L1794 user-verbatim 
 A Walking Skeleton's small size is a satisfied requirement, not an achievement to be scored against a feature-complete codebase; comparing them on quantity is a category error. 
Q: BookMinder is just a Walking Skeleton (as I requested! so it's not a bad thing) -- so you are comparing apples with oranges.
--- day-006 day-006:L1795 user-verbatim 
 A claim about a process's payoff is unfounded until that process has actually been run through a complete cycle — BookMinder had not yet reached the refactor step of the TDD inner loop, so no efficiency conclusion was available. 
Q: Cost improvement claim is unfounded... we didn't even get to the refactoring stage of the TDD's inner loop with unit tests.
--- day-006 day-006:L1796 user-verbatim 
 The author refuses conclusions that flatter his own methodology; his honest report is that the detailed CLAUDE.md process had not yet paid off and the project had been bikeshedding tooling instead. 
Q: Subjectively, I haven't felt the payoff from detailed process description in CLAUDE.md on BookMinder yet -- it was my initial hope, but we got sidetracked and were bikeshedding the development environ
--- day-006 day-006:L1512 user-verbatim 
 Causal attribution requires checking the record the repo already keeps — the answer to "which model built this" was sitting in pyproject.toml's contributors list the whole time. 
Q: you are misinterpreting the Claude 4 cost efficientcy gains, since except day-005, all previous sessions on BookMinder were still done with Sonnet 3.7. You should have noticed that in colaborators.
--- day-007 day-007:L2707-L2708 user-verbatim 
 A test that cannot distinguish between outcomes verifies nothing — a sort assertion over a one-element fixture is decoration, and the honest response is to delete the feature it pretends to cover. 
Q: I think the sort test now doesn't veryfy enything, because we have only single Book in out test Book.plist. I'm not confinced we need the sorting there at all.
--- day-007 day-007:L2708-L2711 user-verbatim 
 Domain semantics must be understood before behavior is built on them — the author refuses to keep a feature whose underlying field he cannot interpret, and reasons out loud about where the real signal lives instead. 
Q: I'm uncertain about the semantics of the updated field in the Book.plist ... I think when working with BookMinder, we would focus on user's interactions with the book. I guess these are store in the S
--- day-007 day-007:L2711-L2713 user-verbatim 
 Spec structure is documentation structure — tests are grouped by the unit they specify, and the author imports Jest/RSpec habits deliberately (shared setup hoisted to the describe, one describe per function) rather than accepting whatever nesting the agent produced. 
Q: in Jest, I would have moved the common setup between `it` to shared `describe` -- must the import of `list_books` be repeated in each `it`?  This brings me to illogical order of these tests
--- day-007 day-007:L7759-L7760 user-verbatim 
 Platform lock-in is a deliberate scope decision, not a defect — a change must not be sold as buying portability the product does not want. 
Q: we're still completely locked to apple platform because that's where Apple Books run. We are not trying to make a cross platform tool!
--- day-007 day-007:L7731-L7732 user-verbatim 
 Verification is demanded proportionally — prove the change against the real data before committing, but skip the ceremony if the evidence already exists. 
Q: can you test locally against real binary Books.plist, before we commit and push, to be sure we handle both? (I saw you ran some ad-hoc test before... You can skip and commit directly if the implementa
--- day-007 day-007:L1238 user-verbatim 
 The provenance of test data is part of the artifact — how a fixture was derived from reality must be written down or the fixture becomes unfalsifiable folklore. 
Q: this is good, but we should document how we prepared the test data in fixture in /docs/fixtures.md to keep track of our thinking later
--- day-008 day-008:L2455 user-verbatim 
 An exploratory phase ends by writing down what was learned and then deliberately discarding the context that produced it; the document, not the conversation, is the durable artifact — and clearing context is itself the test of whether the document is complete. 
Q: Should we actually use `/compact` or `/clear` and then read the apple_books.md to clear our minds before proceeding with the implementation?
--- day-008 day-008:L2428 user-verbatim 
 A document is organized for a reader building understanding in order; content is placed by whose document it is and what the reader knows at that point, not by what is currently on the author's mind. 
Q: I see it's relevant for our next TODO, but how is it usefull to put it at the top od apple_books.md?
--- day-009 day-009:L8039-L8041 user-verbatim 
 BookMinder is a benchmark for the process, not only a utility — the durable artifacts are the story cards and their acceptance tests, with working code as the output an agentic system must derive from them. 
Q: one of the ideas I was playing in my head for this project is to turn it into a benchmark of sorts... the inputs being ATTD specs and the goal of agentic coding systems woudl be to produce the working
--- day-009 day-009:L8222-L8223 user-verbatim 
 Product-owner practice is the missing outer loop — story cards organised as a walk through the system, each expanded into acceptance tests, is the artifact chain worth accumulating, and AI augmentation of an expert PO is a first-class use case. 
Q: In my day job, I am a Product Owner. So, Let's bring in the perspective of Jeff Patton as Described in his book User Stories Mapping.
--- day-009 day-009:L5037-L5038 user-verbatim 
 Test seams should be discovered rather than invented — the author repeatedly points the agent at the shape the code already has instead of accepting new mocking machinery. 
Q: If you look at how we structure our code in library.py for Books.plist and then how we are monkey patching it in spec, isn't that pattern worth following here with DB too? (I have a feeling it might m
--- day-010 day-010:L30 user-verbatim 
 A spec that only passes on the author's machine is not a spec; portability of the acceptance suite is a precondition for the code existing publicly at all. 
Q: This is a pre-requisite for pushing our current code to GitHub, as the
`it_shows_recently_read_books_with_progress` would not work there or on any other
developer's machine.
--- day-010 day-010:L186 user-verbatim 
 A test seam earns its place in production only if it is also a real user-facing capability; the admin use case is what licenses --user, not the testing need. 
Q: Maybe adding a CLI param could be considered a feature: as Administrator I could use
it to explore books by all users on the computer.
--- day-010 day-010:L1083 user-verbatim 
 Environmental facts must be observed, not inferred; the author repeatedly refuses the agent's confident generalisations and runs another experiment on a real machine instead. This is executable-truth reasoning applied to the world outside the repo. 
Q: We don't know whether katka opened Apple Books or of the sdditional structure was
created because she signed into her Apple Account!
--- day-010 day-010:L3304 user-verbatim 
 Test logic has no business in production code; when the agent framed the mixing of test and production concerns as an unavoidable tension, the author rejected the framing and asked why the branch was not confined to the spec fixture. 
Q: What is the test user detection doing in production code? Why isn't this only in the
spec fixture?
--- day-010 day-010:L5911 user-verbatim 
 The highest-yield question about a green suite is why it is green. A mock that ignores the argument under test makes the spec unfalsifiable, and passing a real fixture path through the product's own parameter removes the need to mock at all. 
Q: Since we are now passing the Path as parameter, do we need to monkeypath in
librar_spec the use_test_books or can we just extract the fixtures/Books.plist into
constant and pass it directly?
--- day-011 day-011:L7172 user-verbatim 
 Fixtures are constructions and can only confirm what was built into them; a hypothesis about the world must be tested against the world, i.e. the author's real Apple Books database.

--- day-011 day-011:L9089 user-verbatim 
 Extending a feature must not disturb the assertions that already specify it — the existing expected output stays valid as a prefix, and the new work is specified as the suffix that appears after it. 
Q: We probably should not rewrite the original acceptance test examples and assertions. The format remains valid in the prefix form. We should now add filter
for flag and confirm it contains the expected
--- day-012 day-012:L2255 user-verbatim 
 Domain assumptions are validated against real observed data before any test or fixture is shaped around them — the fixture may not be edited to rescue a hypothesis. 
Q: First validate you assumption against my real Apple Books database.
--- day-012 day-012:L2629 user-verbatim 
 A disproved hypothesis is project knowledge, not waste — the falsification is written into the domain document before work resumes. 
Q: These aren't individual books ZSTATE=5 seems like "Series" -- a new concept that we haven't identified before in our analysis.
This might be worthy an update, a note somewhere in, @docs/apple_books.md
--- day-013 day-013:L1446 user-verbatim 
 BookMinder is a meta-project — building a cognitive exoskeleton while simultaneously assessing the agentic capabilities of the AI building it; the process is as much the product as the CLI is. 
Q: this is quite a meta project. About evolving human agmentation, mental prosthetics and cognitive exoskeleton, while at the same time assessing all of you emerging artifficial intelligences with your n
--- day-013 day-013:L997 user-verbatim 
 When the domain model is unknown, documentation of the evidence comes before any implementation or test-data change — you cannot encode a requirement you have not yet established. 
Q: before we do anything else with the implementation, I would like to be more thorough with our documentation in apple_books.md
--- day-013 day-013:L866 user-verbatim 
 Guessing ahead of the evidence is the cardinal sin of this collaboration; a hypothesis about a foreign schema must be validated against a second independent source before it drives a change. 
Q: You're jumping to conclusions.
--- day-013 day-013:L2936 user-verbatim 
 Observations must be labelled with the environment that produced them — the same app on iPhone and on Mac renders different attribute vocabularies, so an undated, unplaced screenshot is not evidence. 
Q: The original list was compiled from screenshots from iOS Apple Books on the iPhone. This used small tiles display for the books
--- day-014 day-014:L338 user-verbatim 
 Reverse engineering is its own phase with its own exit condition: nothing may be changed in the implementation or the tests until the schema's meaning is verified, because a fix built on an unverified hypothesis is a guess with a green test on top. 
Q: Let's not rush to conclusions. I want to thoroughly verify we have correctly reverse engineered the ZSTATE before we return to fixin the implementation and
tests.
--- day-014 day-014:L340 user-verbatim 
 A hypothesis earns trust only by being probed systematically against the live data, not by being consistent with the notes already written down. 
Q: Do we now have a consistent hypothesis zbout ZSTATE that we can try to verify by systematically probing data?
--- day-014 day-014:L214 user-verbatim 
 Documentation of an external system is a claim about observable reality, so it is validated by checking it item-by-item against the observation (the UI screenshots), never by making it read better. 
Q: We should now meticulously verify the Book states/flags we have
documented in @docs/apple_books.md "#### Previous Section" match exactly what's in the @docs/Previous\ list.jpg and @docs/Previous\ list
--- day-015 day-015:L440-L441 user-verbatim 
 The human is a callable oracle for observations the agent cannot verify; before adopting a more complicated model, spend a turn asking the human to adjudicate the anomalies that motivated it.

--- day-015 day-015:L444-L446 user-verbatim

1	# Persistence — the substrate and the sweep
2	
3	
4	The author will not be your reminder trigger: persistently record everything that exists only in session state and would not survive container restart or compaction, without being prompted.
5	
6	**`.coordination/` is the durable substrate, and it is committed.** How urgent its durability is depends on the environment — see the split below.
7	
8	The substrate's fixed core: `threads.md` (the standing record, structure below) · `tools/` (committed runnable scripts: validators, scanners, versioned swarm scripts). Project-specific corpora, design documents, and work queues live alongside these; keep their map current in `threads.md`. Graduation into docs/ or skills is the author's call.
9	
10	## threads.md — the single standing record
11	
12	Keep these sections live:
13	
14	- **HANDOFF — READ FIRST AFTER COMPACTION** at the very top: current phase state, where artifacts live, how to verify them, what must not be started without his go, and what inputs are pending from him.
15	- **Session goal and meta-goals**, in his framing, attributed.
16	- **Working style rules** — every conduct correction he has made, with his short verbatim phrase attached so the rule keeps its teeth.
17	- **Decisions and authorizations**, dated, including scope grants (what a worker may read) and standing authorizations.
18	- **Open threads**, numbered, each with its blocking condition.
19	- **Parked proposals** — *your* ideas awaiting his go, each with the moment it should resurface, so none is lost in the flood of a long session.
20	- **Review ledger** — his read state per artifact and its ratification status.
21	- **Operations ledger** — live state: what is running, what is stopped, what awaits which decision, with run IDs and script paths.
22	- **Failure modes observed** — your own errors, with root cause, as meta-lab data.
23	
24	## The sweep
25	
26	**The persistence sweep is machinery, not discipline.** At every watchdog firing, every task-notification, and before ending any substantial turn: diff "what exists only in conversation context" against "what is committed," and commit the delta. Embed this instruction in the watchdog trigger's own prompt so it fires by machinery. This is the stickiness law applied to yourself: corrections shipped as automation stick; as prose they only partly stick.
27	
28	Also persist: scripts you wrote (validators, scanners, workflow scripts) into `.coordination/tools/`, and design documents that carry policy later phases must inherit.
29	
30	## Git and commit conventions — evergreen (every environment)
31	
32	- Stage files explicitly by name. Never `git add .`.
33	- Use `git mv` for moves.
34	- Commit messages explain **why**, referencing the decision or directive that motivated the change.
35	- Follow the environment's mandated git conventions — commit trailers and branch targets arrive with the harness or per-session directives; honor them, do not restate them here.
36	- Commit after each meaningful state change — commit cadence is evergreen; PUSH cadence is environment-conditional (below).
37	- When a repo file must be reconstructed from history, prefer a checkpoint restore (`git rm -r` + `git checkout <sha> -- path`) over piecemeal patching, and verify the restoration by running the suite and grepping for the specific artifacts that were supposed to return.
38	
39	## Environment-conditional: push policy and memory
40	
41	- **Ephemeral infra (remote cloud container; CI such as GitHub Actions): push after each meaningful state change.** The workspace can be wiped at any time; pushing is the only durability, and the pushed repo is the only cross-session memory (remote containers have no auto-memory and no user-global CLAUDE.md — verify rather than assume). If a permission layer blocks a combined `commit && push`, run them as separate commands rather than abandoning the push.
42	- **Local machine: commit per the evergreen conventions, but PUSHING IS THE AUTHOR'S DECISION — do not push without his word.** The workspace persists; there is no wipe pressure, and he reserves the push call for himself.
43	- Determine which regime you are in at session start, before adopting a push cadence.

# Apple Books Data Sources

This document describes the data sources used by Apple Books on macOS and how BookMinder accesses them.

## Overview

Apple Books stores data across multiple files and databases in different container directories. Understanding these data sources is crucial for extracting book metadata, reading progress, and activity information.

## Container Directories

Apple Books uses sandboxed containers to store its data:

- **com.apple.BKAgentService**: Contains the book files and basic catalog
- **com.apple.iBooksX**: Contains databases for reading progress, activity, and UI state

## Data Sources

### 1. Books.plist

**Location**: `/Users/{user}/Library/Containers/com.apple.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/Books.plist`

**Purpose**: Primary book catalog with metadata

**Key Fields**:
- `itemName`: Book title
- `artistName`: Author name
- `path`: Relative path to EPUB file
- `updateDate`: Last modification date
- `BKPercentComplete`: Only present for **finished books** (always 1.0 = 100%)

**Important Discovery**:
- Contains all books in library (179 total in test case)
- Only 22 books have `BKPercentComplete` field (12% of library)
- All books with `BKPercentComplete` show 1.0 (100% complete)
- Books without this field are either unread or partially read
- **Does NOT contain actual reading progress for books in progress**

### 2. BKLibrary SQLite Database

**Location Pattern**: `/Users/{user}/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/BKLibrary-*.sqlite`

**Note**: The filename contains variable numbers (e.g., `BKLibrary-1-091020131601.sqlite`) that change between installations. Use glob pattern matching to locate.

**Purpose**: Complete library database with reading progress and activity

**Key Table**: `ZBKLIBRARYASSET`

**Critical Fields for Reading Progress**:
- `ZTITLE`: Book title
- `ZAUTHOR`: Author name
- `ZASSETID`: Asset identifier (matches Books.plist keys)
- `ZREADINGPROGRESS`: Float value (0.0 to 1.0) representing actual reading progress
- `ZLASTOPENDATE`: Timestamp when book was last opened (Apple reference date)
- `ZISFINISHED`: Integer indicating if book is finished (1 = finished, 0 = not finished)
- `ZDATEFINISHED`: Timestamp when book was finished
- `ZCREATIONDATE`: When book was added to library

**Additional Important Fields**:
- `ZISSAMPLE`: Integer indicating if book is a sample (1 = sample, 0 = full book)
- `ZCONTENTTYPE`: Integer indicating content type (likely: 1 = Book, 3 = PDF)
- `ZPATH`: Path to the book file (relative to Books directory)
- `ZFILESIZE`: Size of the book file in bytes
- `ZSTATE`: Integer indicating download/availability state
- `ZGENRE`: Book genre/category
- `ZKIND`: Content kind (e.g., "ebook", "pdf")
- `ZPAGECOUNT`: Number of pages in the book
- `ZISEPHEMERAL`: Integer indicating temporary status

"""
Quick validation script for skills - minimal version

import sys
import re
import yaml
from pathlib import Path

# Directories whose contents are not packaged as part of the skill, so any
# SKILL.md inside them shouldn't count toward the single-SKILL.md check below.
# Mirrors package_skill.py: __pycache__ and node_modules are excluded at any
# depth, while evals is only excluded at the skill root.
EXCLUDED_DIR_PARTS = {'__pycache__', 'node_modules'}
ROOT_EXCLUDED_DIR_PARTS = {'evals'}


def _counts_as_skill_md(rel_path):
    """True if a SKILL.md at rel_path (relative to the skill root) would be packaged."""
    dir_parts = rel_path.parts[:-1]
    if any(part in EXCLUDED_DIR_PARTS for part in dir_parts):
        return False
    if dir_parts and dir_parts[0] in ROOT_EXCLUDED_DIR_PARTS:
        return False
    return True


def validate_skill(skill_path):
    """Basic validation of a skill"""
    skill_path = Path(skill_path)

    # Check SKILL.md exists
    skill_md = skill_path / 'SKILL.md'
    if not skill_md.exists():
        return False, "SKILL.md not found"

    # A skill must contain exactly one SKILL.md, at <folder>/SKILL.md. Extra
    # (nested) SKILL.md files are rejected on upload: the Skills API and claude.ai
    # accept exactly one per skill — only Claude Code's filesystem loads nested
    # ones. package_skill produces an upload-bound .skill, so block here rather
    # than ship an artifact that's guaranteed to fail on upload.
    skill_md_files = [
        p for p in skill_path.rglob('SKILL.md')
        if _counts_as_skill_md(p.relative_to(skill_path))
    ]
    if len(skill_md_files) > 1:
        extras = sorted(
            str(p.relative_to(skill_path)) for p in skill_md_files
            if p.resolve() != skill_md.resolve()
        )
        return False, (
            f"Found {len(skill_md_files)} SKILL.md files, but a skill must contain "
            f"exactly one at <folder>/SKILL.md. The Skills API and claude.ai reject "
            f"multiple on upload (only Claude Code's filesystem loads nested skills). "
            f"Extra: {', '.join(extras)}.\n"
            "  - Separate skills: package each on its own, or build a plugin "
            "(skills/<name>/SKILL.md).\n"
            "  - Supporting docs: rename to non-SKILL.md files (e.g. references/<topic>.md).\n"
            "  - Swept in by mistake: package only the one skill directory."
        )

    # Read and validate frontmatter
    content = skill_md.read_text()
    if not content.startswith('---'):
        return False, "No YAML frontmatter found"

    # Extract frontmatter
    match = re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---', content, re.DOTALL)
    if not match:
        return False, "Invalid frontmatter format"

    frontmatter_text = match.group(1)

    # Parse YAML frontmatter
    try:
        frontmatter = yaml.safe_load(frontmatter_text)
        if not isinstance(frontmatter, dict):
            return False, "Frontmatter must be a YAML dictionary"

# Goals and history — what BookMinder is for

## Destination and core question

- **B-01 — Destination.** An MCP tool for discussing books with Claude: the author reads on his iPhone and wants to talk with an LLM about the book he is reading, its last chapter, and the highlights made since the last conversation. CLI first, deliberately — the author knows CLI design and TDD/BDD cold, while MCP was unfamiliar territory; the CLI is the walking skeleton of the broader vision.
- **B-02 — Core question.** Can an LLM be a good pair programmer? The author had no colleagues to pair with; this project is the experiment. The method is the point: executable specifications nail verifiable invariants, and the art is slicing the problem and designing specs with minimal coupling to implementation — London school, GOOS lineage. The root principle everything else derives from: the spec's job is nailing requirements in a falsifiable way. Executable specification, GOOS layers, enforced layer separation, and delegation contracts all follow from falsifiability — a hierarchy, not parallel motivations.
- **B-03 — Why Apple Books as testbed.** Deliberately chosen because the Apple Books database schema is undocumented and evolves with each macOS release. That makes the project a test of long-term software evolution and maintenance — the opposite of one-shotting problems the model already knows from pretraining.
- **B-04 — Book-grounding motivation (product feeds process).** Pretrained simulacra of TDD/BDD experts proved shallow caricatures — skewed, non-actionable summaries of real positions. A core BookMinder motivation is giving the model access to full books as consultation material, so actionable principles can be extracted from primary sources that did not survive pretraining summarization. The failure-mode name for the thing this defeats: simulacra-shallowness.
- **B-05 — The project is a vehicle and a benchmark.** The real object of study is whether an AI coding agent can hold a strict ATDD process as a pair programmer; process artifacts are therefore deliverables, not cruft. The durable artifact chain is story cards expanded into acceptance tests, with working code as the output an agentic system must derive from them — the author (a Product Owner by day job, working in Jeff Patton's User Story Mapping tradition) has long intended the project to double as a benchmark of agentic coding systems.

## History

- **B-06 — BookMind, the predecessor.** BookMind implemented most of the original vision — EPUB parsing, highlight extraction, markdown export, a working CLI, 40 passing tests. It was not a failure. The fork to BookMinder was motivated by process, cost, and code quality: the agent took too much unrequested initiative and produced a sprawling codebase at high cost. Never describe BookMind as broken software, and never score BookMinder against BookMind on size, coverage, or feature count — BookMinder is a walking skeleton by explicit request, so the comparison measures the choice, not the outcome. `ORIGINAL_VISION.md` is a copy of BookMind's first README (verify with `git show 64dc71b:README.md` in the BookMind repo context), not a BookMinder-specific document.
- **B-07 — Scope discipline is the founding constraint.** BookMinder exists specifically to stop the agent from running ahead with its own creative ideas. The scope is the GOOS walking skeleton plus whatever the story cards ask for; add no capability the author has not asked for. CLAUDE.md is the instrument of that constraint.
- **B-08 — Apple-only by design.** Apple Books is the product's entire subject. Never propose, justify, or advertise a change on cross-platform grounds; CI pins macOS.
- **B-09 — Timeline in brief.** Summer 2025: intense development — a gold-standard ATDD era, then a process lapse after commit 6f786cc (features landed without proper ATDD; the repair backlog for this still stands) — ending in the author's burnout from holding process discipline for models that knew the process but could not perform it (knowing vs performing is the key distinction). ~1 year dormant. 2026-08: reevaluation sessions on cloud infrastructure — no new feature code; the 2025 session diary was mined into a rules corpus, the spec tree was restored wholesale to its pre-reorg concern-based form, commit-after-RED was restored to CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md became symlinks to CLAUDE.md, and this skill was compiled.
- **B-10 — The stickiness law.** Corrections shipped as automation (hooks, validators, CI) stick; shipped as prose they only partly stick. The author rates Claude Code hooks the most valuable CC innovation for exactly this reason: enforcement via automation, not prose. When a rule keeps being violated, the durable fix is machinery, and the open experiment question is how much harness enforcement discipline requires once skills are in place.

# Repo geography, backlog, and fixture architecture

## Orientation

- **B-20 — Cheapest grounding.** The production package is tiny (~290 lines: `bookminder/cli.py` + `bookminder/apple_books/library.py`) — read it whole before any task; it is cheaper than guessing. The behavior spec of the whole system is `pytest --spec`. Feature entry chain: `bookminder/cli.py` → `bookminder/apple_books/library.py`; everything else is docs, fixtures, or process. Never run unfiltered `find .` or repo-wide line counts — exclude caches, any vendored venv, and `claude-dev-log-diary/` from every listing or metric.
- **B-21 — Land mines.** `claude-dev-log-diary/` (~12M of hand-curated session transcripts) is permission-gated: never read, grep, commit, or surface it — including indirectly via `git diff`/`git show`/`git log -p` — without explicit user consent, and a grant is scoped to the exact excerpt and manner named (targeted range reads in the foreground; never whole-file reads, never background-subagent greps). One day-file may contain several sessions (`^claude` marks each start) and only the session-end cost figure is valid. `docs/ui/apple/` holds ~2.5M of binary screenshots — reference by path, never Read. `specs/apple_books/fixtures/All_Books*.swift` (~240K each) are grep-only and deliberately untracked pending curation — do not gitignore them and never stage them. Fixture `.sqlite` files are binary — query with `sqlite3`, never Read. The `./xs` symlink resolves into the forbidden diary directory: execute it as the documented tool, do not read it as a file. Zero-byte fixture files (`401429854.epub`, corrupted_db_user's plist+sqlite) are intentional — that is the fixture's point, not damage to repair.
- **B-22 — Spec tree layout.** Specs are concern-based at HEAD: `specs/cli_spec.py`, `specs/cli_formatting_spec.py`, `specs/apple_books/library_spec.py`, `specs/apple_books/library_integration_spec.py`, with fixtures co-located under `specs/apple_books/fixtures/`. A 2025 four-layer reorg (`unit/integration/acceptance/e2e`) was reverted wholesale in 2026-08 by checkpoint restore; those directories may linger as untracked `__pycache__` residue only — they are not tracked structure (confirm with `git ls-files specs/`). Coverage caveat: `specs/cli_spec.py` drives the CLI via `subprocess` (`sys.executable -m bookminder`, cli_spec.py:19-38), and pytest-cov does not follow child processes — never read a coverage gap in subprocess-exercised code as evidence it is untested.

## Backlog and stories

- **B-23 — Backlog practice.** Stories are YAML cards under `stories/` in story-map columns: `discover` covers listing, filtering, admin access, and error handling; `access` is controlling the Apple Books app; `review` is highlights and notes; `export` is text extraction. Every card carries a mandatory `status` from the vocabulary CLAUDE.md `<backlog_management>` defines — status only, no priority/assignee metadata (YAGNI). TODO.md's Discover Column is a bare list of story paths in implementation order: the order is the plan, so take the next story in order rather than offering a menu, and keep the list free of emoji, numbering, and per-item rationale. Completed Features is an immutable record of the journey — never reorder or remove entries; annotate a reopened story in place (`[REOPENED: ...]`); refactorings are not listed there (user-visible stories only); a doc deletion gets a one-line breadcrumb with its commit hash. Parked backlog items must carry enough of the HOW (mechanism, trigger, expected behavior) that a fresh session can execute them without asking. Declared statuses can lie — verify against implementation and `git log` before acting on them (see current-state page).

## Settled design decisions in the code

- **B-24 — CLI shape.** `main` is a Click group; `list` is a subgroup declared `@main.group(name="list")` on a function named `list_cmd` — never name the function `list`, which shadows the builtin and breaks `list[Book]` annotations at import time (fix name collisions at the source, not with deprecated typing aliases). Subcommands `recent` and `all` share options via the `with_common_list_options` decorator (Click does not inherit group options). Filter vocabulary: one repeatable `--filter` option whose values are attribute names with `!` negation (`cloud`, `!cloud`, `sample`, `!sample`) — `!` and not `-` because Click parses a leading `-` as an option; filters are orthogonal to list commands (nothing in Apple Books' UI makes them command-specific). `list recent` deliberately replicates Apple's Continue section so that an agent consuming the future MCP surface and the human looking at the app share one frame of reference. `--user` is simultaneously a real admin feature (examine another user's books) and the test seam — the admin use case is what licenses it in production. The CLI owns no domain knowledge: it passes the raw `--user` string and filter through to the library and delegates path resolution and querying there.
- **B-25 — The Book type.** One `Book` TypedDict with `NotRequired` optional fields; never a parallel type for a variant that adds a field. Only `title` and `author` are required — `path` and `updated` are `NotRequired` because the SQLite path cannot supply them (see domain page). TypedDict is a static annotation only: it produces a plain dict, no attribute access, no runtime key enforcement.

## Fixture architecture

- **B-26 — Synthetic $HOME personas and the front-door seam.** Integration fixtures are synthetic home-directory trees under `specs/apple_books/fixtures/users/<persona>/` replicating Apple's container layout path-for-path. Each persona encodes a container state observed on a real machine: `test_reader` (full library), `fresh_books_user` (all containers, empty plist, empty-schema sqlite), `legacy_books_user` (containers but no BKLibrary directory), `never_opened_user` (only the OS-created `com.apple.iBooksX` container — no BKAgentService, no plist, no sqlite), `corrupted_db_user` (zero-byte plist and sqlite; note a corruption scenario needs the full container present or the plist check fires before the sqlite error). The seam is the front door: `--user` with an absolute path is used verbatim as the home directory, a bare name resolves to `/Users/<name>`, `None` to `Path.home()` — exactly three cases, specced in `library._get_user_path`, no falsy-string case. Specs must pass absolute fixture paths (a relative path is treated as a username and silently rewritten). This seam exists because fixtures through the product's own parameter exercise the real path-construction code, where patching a private module name would bypass it; the older module-constant seam (`BKLIBRARY_DB_FILE`-style) survives only with its known limitation — it is an in-process substitution resolved at import time and cannot cross a subprocess boundary.
- **B-27 — Fixture data discipline.** The fixture database carries the real schema verbatim — dump `.schema ZBKLIBRARYASSET` from a live database, never hand-write a schema. Rows are copies of real, complete book records: populate only with `specs/apple_books/fixtures/copy_book_to_fixture.sh` (ATTACH DATABASE + explicit column list minus Z_PK, generated from `PRAGMA table_info`), never hand-written or hand-edited SQL — an invented or edited row encodes the agent's beliefs exactly where the spec is supposed to be falsifiable. If a needed state does not exist, the author adjusts a real book in his library and it gets copied. Use the existing scripts (`create_fixture.sh` creates, `copy_book_to_fixture.sh` populates); if a script fails, debug the script. Scripts never delete — cleanup is a deliberate human act. Script rules: parameter variable is `FIXTURE_USER`, never `USERNAME` (a zsh special parameter that silently shadows the argument — this bug is fixed at HEAD, copy_book_to_fixture.sh:8); SQL-escape titles by doubling quotes; locate the fixture DB by the same `BKLibrary-*.sqlite` glob production uses; root every path at PROJECT_ROOT and verify the resolved path before the first write (a swapped path once planted a stray fixture inside the real Apple Books directory). Document how each fixture was derived in `docs/test_fixtures.md` in the same commit. Preserve intentionally-empty directories with a single `.gitkeep` at the leaf. Prefer extending `test_reader` over new personas unless a test needs isolation. After any fixture change, verify through the product: `python -m bookminder list recent --user <absolute fixture path>`.
- **B-28 — Fixture census freshness.** Never rely on a remembered census of what `test_reader` contains — earlier remembered censuses went stale when books were swapped. The census truth is one query away: `sqlite3 "specs/apple_books/fixtures/users/test_reader/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/BKLibrary-fixture.sqlite" "SELECT ZTITLE, ZSTATE, ZISSAMPLE, ZREADINGPROGRESS FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET"`. Lore: the zero-byte `401429854.epub` placeholder is "Growing Object-Oriented Software, Guided by Tests" — the project's canonical known book, named in ORIGINAL_VISION.md.
- **B-29 — Real DB vs fixtures.** Exploration of Apple Books behavior runs read-only against a real database — fixtures can only confirm what was built into them; when reality shows a new case worth capturing, it gets copied into the fixture. This cloud environment has no live Apple Books library, so any exploration here runs against fixtures only: say so explicitly and mark conclusions provisional. Fixtures freeze time — any recency-window behavior must be specified with controlled time, or the snapshot silently ages out of the window.
- **B-30 — Toolchain and environment.** Python pinned `==3.13.*` (pyproject.toml:11) — pinning, not a permissive floor, because reproducibility across machines depends on one interpreter; uv + ruff + mypy, setuptools backend; ruff `target-version = "py312"` (pyproject.toml:71) stays until the pinned ruff accepts py313. Run tests from the venv: `source .venv/bin/activate && pytest` (`uvx bookminder` fails — unpublished; bare `uv run` re-downloads CPython). The cloud environment may arrive with no `.venv` — provision with `uv venv && uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`. When ruff disagrees between shell and hook, compare `.pre-commit-config.yaml`'s pinned `rev:` against `ruff --version` in the venv. `check-toml` stays in pre-commit — an invalid pyproject once passed an all-green run and broke the second machine.
- **B-31 — Repo maintenance principles.** Exactly one source of truth per concern; a migration deletes the superseded file inside itself. Never invent identity metadata — the author is Pavol Vaskovic (pali@pali.sk); ask or leave blank. An untested causal claim does not go into docs: if you assert X is required, remove X and show the failure first, and never document a command until you have run it and shown it working. Judge any document by whether it is referred back to and changes behavior on this project — retrospective meta-analysis docs fail both tests and the author calls them slop. README bash snippets carry no inline comments (readers copy-paste them); explanation goes in the prose above.

# Apple Books domain lore

Verification status is honest here: **verified@tree** = encoded in the current code/fixtures and exercised by the suite; **observed-2025** = established against a live library in 2025, needs a fresh live-DB probe before you lean on it; **hypothesis** = open, never settled. This environment has no live Apple Books database — nothing here can be re-verified in place, only against fixtures.

## Data sources

- **B-40 — Two sandboxed containers (verified@tree, encoded at library.py:17-25).** `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/` holds `Books.plist` (the catalogue) beside per-book `<numeric-id>.epub` items. `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/` holds the library database. Discover the database by glob — `BKLibrary-*.sqlite` — never by literal filename: the numeric segments (e.g. `BKLibrary-1-091020131601.sqlite`) are per-install artifacts.
- **B-41 — Plist vs database roles (observed-2025; the split is load-bearing for the whole design).** `Books.plist` is a catalogue: `itemName`, `artistName`, `path`, `updateDate`. Its `BKPercentComplete` appears only on finished books (always 1.0) — it cannot express in-progress reading. Real reading state lives in the database table `ZBKLIBRARYASSET` (`ZREADINGPROGRESS`, `ZLASTOPENDATE`, `ZISFINISHED`, `ZDATEFINISHED`, `ZCREATIONDATE`). The database is the authoritative catalogue: the plist omits cloud-only titles, so absence from the plist proves nothing about library membership, and a title's absence is never evidence of cloud status. `updateDate` in the plist is publisher-revision metadata, not reading activity — BookMinder cares about the user's relationship to the book, which lives in the database. Books lazy-download from iCloud: a book in the catalogue with no file on disk is a valid library entry — never filter books by on-disk file existence.
- **B-42 — Apple epoch (verified@tree, library.py:11,65-66).** Core Data timestamps count seconds from 2001-01-01 UTC, not 1970 — raw values look like plausible Unix times and are silently ~31 years wrong without the `APPLE_EPOCH` offset.

## The ZSTATE census — the project's signature reflex

- **B-43 — ZSTATE is a small enum whose census must be re-taken, not recalled.** Every single-value story ever told about ZSTATE ("5 means cloud", "5 means series", "3 is the cloud value") was contradicted by the next batch of real rows; books showing the UI cloud icon were observed at ZSTATE 1, 3, and 6. The working set the code encodes (observed-2025, at library.py:76-77): **1** = present locally (including downloaded samples), **3** = cloud book, **6** = cloud sample not yet downloaded. **ZSTATE 5 is an OPEN HYPOTHESIS, not a verified mapping**: earlier research recorded it as "Series entity / unowned series book" (linked by ZSERIESID, with the entity's ZTITLE being the series name), and `docs/apple_books.md` still asserts that as verified — but a later systematic re-probe observed 5 only as a *second* row for a title that already had a 3, which the series story does not predict. Until a live-DB re-census settles it, treat 5 as unmapped and the docs' "Verified ZSTATE Mappings" section as over-claiming. The method that produced every real breakthrough here: enumerate all distinct values DB-first and characterize each, instead of reasoning UI-first from the values already seen.
- **B-44 — Sample detection is a composite predicate (verified@tree, library.py:77).** `is_sample` = `ZSTATE = 6 OR ZISSAMPLE = 1`. `ZISSAMPLE = 0` is never proof a book is not a sample — unmistakable UI samples carried `ZISSAMPLE = 0` and were identifiable only by `ZSTATE = 6`. Lifecycle (hypothesis, explains the composite): a store sample enters the library as `ZSTATE=6, ZISSAMPLE=0` (cloud sample) and becomes `ZSTATE=1, ZISSAMPLE=1` once opened/downloaded. ZSTATE 6 is the common case, downloaded samples the edge case — cover both. Per-title sample observations flipped between probes in 2025 (the same title read `ZISSAMPLE 0` one session and `1` another), so any per-title claim needs a freshness stamp and a re-run query, never a citation of notes. Cloud display vs cloud filter diverge at HEAD (verified@tree): `is_cloud` = `ZSTATE in (3, 6)` (library.py:76) but `--filter cloud` matches `ZSTATE = 3` only (library.py:154-159) — a cloud sample displays ☁️ yet is excluded by the cloud filter; know this before "fixing" either side without a spec.
- **B-45 — ZCONTENTTYPE is unverified (hypothesis).** Likely 1 = book (EPUB), 3 = PDF — hedged until re-verified on a live database. `docs/apple_books.md` states it hedged at line 60 and flat at lines 114-115; the hedged form governs.
- **B-46 — Column facts.** `ZTITLE` is not a key (observed-2025): one title can have multiple rows (duplicate rows at different ZSTATEs, even under two author strings), so any title lookup must handle and explain duplicates or detection becomes non-deterministic. `ZISFINISHED = 1` is the sole definition of finished (observed-2025): finished books exist below 100% progress, so never require `ZREADINGPROGRESS = 1.0`. `ZLASTOPENDATE` was never NULL for rows with progress > 0 (observed-2025, 221 rows, 0 nulls) — the basis for not guarding it; re-verify before adding or removing guards.
- **B-47 — Samples and `list recent` (hypothesis).** Apple Books appears never to populate `ZREADINGPROGRESS` for samples — a sample's reading position was traced to a type-3 annotation in the AEAnnotation database instead. Since `list recent` filters on `ZREADINGPROGRESS > 0`, sample filtering there is structurally near-empty; library-wide sample listing belongs on `list all`.
- **B-48 — "Want to Read" is unresolved (hypothesis).** Composition held as unread-or-sample (`ZREADINGPROGRESS = 0` and not finished, OR sample) for all observed titles, but its ordering was never established — the recorded ZCREATIONDATE conclusion rests on a known arithmetic error. The list is computed by Apple, not marked by the user: document observed database behavior, never inferred user intent, and say "unknown" when the mechanism is unknown.

## Environment facts

- **B-49 — Container lifecycle (observed-2025 on real machines).** `com.apple.iBooksX` is created at macOS account setup; `com.apple.BKAgentService`, `Books.plist`, and the `BKLibrary-*.sqlite` (with 0 rows) are all created together on first launch of Apple Books — no Apple ID required. Reading another user's `~/Library` requires sudo; a plain `--user <name>` run fails with PermissionError. These states are exactly what the fixture personas encode.
- **B-50 — Plist mechanics.** `Books.plist` stores `Books` as an ARRAY of dicts — a dict-keyed-by-id variant parses without error and silently yields zero books (verified@tree: the code guards for list shape, library.py:85-86). Read with `plistlib.load(open(path, "rb"))` — it auto-detects binary and XML; never shell out to `plutil -convert`. For human/agent exploration, render plists as Swift literals: `plutil -convert swift -o out.swift Books.plist` — far more token-efficient than XML; that is what the `All_Books*.swift` dumps are.
- **B-51 — Path correlation is an open problem (verified@tree, library.py:73).** The book file path exists only in `Books.plist`; the database has no usable path, so `_row_to_book` sets `path=""` pending a `ZASSETID`-keyed correlation between the two sources. This is acknowledged design debt, not an oversight.

## Working the database

- **B-52 — Query discipline.** Answer one-off questions with the `sqlite3` CLI directly — no throwaway .py scripts in the tree, no print-debugging through production code. Use targeted column lists, never `SELECT *` (blurb columns flood the context). Parameterize titles with `?` placeholders — hand-escaping apostrophes ("What's Our Problem?") fails repeatedly. When a diacritics-bearing title returns nothing, retry `LIKE` on the longest ASCII-only prefix before concluding the row is absent — the shell round-trip, not the database, is what fails. When probing N items with the same shape, batch with `IN (...)`.
- **B-53 — docs/apple_books.md epistemic status.** It is the captured output of the reverse-engineering phase — a running record of guesses about a schema Apple does not document. It is the thing under test, never the reference: verify any attribute row-by-row against the UI screenshots in `docs/ui/apple/` and a live query, never against the doc's own prose. Editing rules the author enforces: the doc stays descriptive of storage (no SQL that prescribes a feature's filtering strategy); every SQL query lives in the single Database-to-UI-Mapping section other sections link to (two copies of one query is how it contradicted itself); UI quirks (cloud samples rendered "1%") are documented but never replicated in the implementation; screenshots are committed into docs/ and referenced inline next to the claims they support, each labelled with the platform that produced it (iPhone tiles and macOS list views use different attribute vocabularies — macOS "Complete" is a long-form percentage, not a status); preserve the section's existing segmentation when updating contents.

State claims rot. This page names where truth lives and which decisions are genuinely open; when it conflicts with the tree, the tree wins — then update this page.

- **B-60 — Read state, don't recall it.** System behavior: `pytest --spec`. Backlog and order: `TODO.md` + `stories/*/*.yaml` status fields. Session/phase state of the 2026 reevaluation: the HANDOFF section at the top of `.coordination/threads.md`. Domain reference: `docs/apple_books.md` with the epistemic hedges from the domain page applied.

- **B-61 — The dead plist API.** `library.list_books` / `find_book_by_title` are integration-tested but have zero callers in `cli.py`, and README's Usage section (README.md:53-58) shows them called without the now-required `user_home` argument — broken as written. No user ruling exists; either way the README sample must change. Do not delete or spec this API without the author's pick.

Underlying cause: dual bookkeeping between TODO.md and story cards. Practical rule now: never trust a declared status — verify against implementation and `git log` before acting.
- **B-63 — The unspecified borrow.** `cli.py` imports `SUPPORTED_FILTERS` from the library (cli.py:10) — the CLI-borrows-library-vocabulary contract — but no spec asserts the identity; `specs/apple_books/library_spec.py:21` asserts set equality only, so `cli.py` could grow its own matching literal and nothing would fail. Proposed one-line spec exists (`assert cli.SUPPORTED_FILTERS is library.SUPPORTED_FILTERS`, author found the syntax reasonable) — fold into the first repair story, do not add it outside one.

# BookMinder — Project Memory

BookMinder is a Python 3.13 CLI (heading for MCP) that reads a user's Apple Books library — macOS-only by design — built as a live experiment in whether an LLM can be a good pair programmer under strict outside-in ATDD. The process is as much the product as the code: story cards, acceptance specs, and commit grammar are deliverables. The production package is ~290 lines (`bookminder/cli.py` → `bookminder/apple_books/library.py`); the suite under `specs/` is the system's documentation (`pytest --spec`).

This skill is the project's cross-session memory — the environment has none, the repo is the only substrate. Facts here carry their WHY and their verification status; where state can rot, the page points at the command or file that holds truth instead of restating it.

Sibling skills: `tdd-bdd` carries the process discipline; CLAUDE.md is always loaded and owns the build commands and constitution. This skill does not repeat them.

## Page map

- What the project is FOR, why Apple Books, the BookMind prehistory, burnout and the 2026 reevaluation, the benchmark ambition → `references/goals-and-history.md`
- Working in the tree: land mines (the permission-gated diary, huge fixtures), spec layout, backlog/story practice, settled CLI design decisions, fixture personas and the front-door `--user` seam, fixture data discipline, toolchain → `references/repo-geography-and-fixtures.md`
- Anything touching Apple Books data: containers, Books.plist vs BKLibrary sqlite, the Apple epoch, ZSTATE/ZISSAMPLE/ZCONTENTTYPE with verification status, the re-take-the-census reflex, query discipline, docs/apple_books.md's epistemic status → `references/apple-books-domain.md`
- Before judging or changing repo state: where truth lives, the open author decisions (dead plist API, story-status split-brain, unspecified SUPPORTED_FILTERS borrow), ledgered doc rot, the .coordination substrate → `references/current-state-and-open-decisions.md`

## Invariants that never wait for a page load

- Never enter `claude-dev-log-diary/` without the author's explicit, scoped permission — including via `git diff`/`git show`.
- Never propose features, platforms, or "improvements" the author has not asked for; scope discipline is the project's founding constraint.
- Apple Books schema claims are hypotheses until re-verified against a live database; re-take the census, never recall it.
- Declared story statuses and doc claims can lie; verify against the tree and `git log` before acting.
- Nothing an agent produces is repo rule until the author ratifies it.
